title: Novel Atomic Force Microscopy Based Biopanning for Isolation of Morphology Specific Reagents against TDP-43 Variants in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
protocol: Perform all phage production processes in a biosafety cabinet.
Culture bacteria stocks of Tomlinson I and J libraries and Sheets library in 200 ml of 2xYT containing 1% glucose and 100 μg/ml ampicillin on a shaker at 37 °C until OD600 is 0.4.
Add 8 x 10^11 KM13 helper phage to Tomlinson I and J libraries.
Incubate the cultures with helper phages for 30 min at 37 °C without shaking.
Centrifuge the cultures at 3,000 x g for 10 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 ml of 2xYT containing 0.1% glucose, 100 μg/ml ampicillin, and 50 μg/ml kanamycin.
Incubate the cultures overnight at 30 °C with shaking.
Spin the cultures for 30 min at 3,300 x g the following day.
Add 50 ml of PEG 8000 in 2.5 M NaCl to the supernatant from each library and incubate on ice for 1 hr.
After PEG precipitation, spin the solutions again for 30 min at 3,300 x g.
Add 1-2 ml of PBS to the cell pellet.
Transfer the mixture to microcentrifuge tubes.
Incubate phage particles on ice for 1 hour.
Mix phage particles occasionally during incubation.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 11,600 x g.
Collect the supernatant and store at -80°C.
Transfer a small volume of phage particles from three libraries to microcentrifuge tubes.
Titer each library individually using TG1 cells.
Grow TG1 cells to an OD600 of 0.4.
Add 990 μl of PBS to six microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 10 μl of the phage particles to the first tube and mix.
Remove 10 μl from the first tube and add to the second tube, repeat for remaining four tubes.
Add 200 μl of TG1 cells to six tubes.
Add 10 μl of each of the six phage dilutions to these tubes.
Allow phage particles to infect for 30 minutes at 37°C without shaking.
Plate 100 μl of infected cells on Luria-Bertani agar plates with 100 μg/ml ampicillin.
Incubate overnight at 37°C.
Determine the pfu/ml using the number of visible colonies.
Add 4 ml of 1 mg/ml BSA solution in PBS to 12 immunotubes.
Incubate tubes O/N at 4 °C.
Combine 1 x 10^12 phage particles from each of the three libraries.
Discard the BSA solution from the first tube.
Wash the first tube 2-3 times with PBS.
Add the combined phage libraries to the washed first tube.
Incubate for 30 min at RT on the rotator.
Collect unbound phages.
Repeat step 2.1.3 with the second immunotube.
Add collected phages from previous step to the second immunotube.
Repeat step 2.1.4.
Repeat steps 2.1.3-2.1.4 for remaining 10 tubes of BSA solution and unbound phage.
Use AFM to verify removal of all BSA phage binders.
Add 10 μl of phage from step 2.1.2 to 10 μg/ml of BSA on cleaved mica.
Add 10 μl of remaining phage after step 2.1.7 to 10 μg/ml of BSA on cleaved mica.
Allow purified alpha-synuclein to aggregate for at least 7 days.
Prepare 4 immunotubes with 500 μg/ml of aggregated alpha-synuclein in PBS.
Prepare 4 additional immunotubes with 100 μg/ml of aggregated alpha-synuclein in PBS.
Incubate all prepared immunotubes overnight at 4 °C.
Discard the solution from one tube containing 500 μg/ml of aggregated alpha-synuclein.
Wash the discarded tube with PBS.
Add phage library collected after 12 rounds of negative panning with BSA to the washed tube.
Incubate the tube for 30 min at room temperature on a rotator.
Collect unbound phages from the incubated tube.
Repeat steps using remaining tubes containing 500 μg/ml of aggregated alpha-synuclein and then those with 100 μg/ml, using phage collected after each step.
Add STEN buffer to human brain tissue.
Homogenize the mixture at 24,000 rpm for 1 min.
Centrifuge samples at 3,000 rpm and collect supernatant.
Prepare two immunotubes with 2 ml of 50 μg/ml of human brain tissue in PBS.
Incubate the prepared tubes overnight at 4 °C.
Repeat steps involving negative panning against alpha-synuclein for healthy human brain tissue using unbound phage collected after negative panning against alpha-synuclein.
Immunoprecipitate healthy TDP-43 protein from healthy human brain tissue.
Carry out rounds of negative panning on mica surfaces.
Incubate the first mica with ~100 μl of 5 μg/ml immunoprecipitated protein for 5-10 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash the mica 5 times with 0.1% PBS with Tween 20 (PBST).
Add ~100 μl of phage after negative panning against healthy brain tissue to the mica.
Incubate for 5-10 min at RT.
Carry out step 2.4.3 using the second mica halfway through step 2.4.5 incubation.
Collect the phage from step 2.4.5 and wash the mica 5 times with 0.1% PBST.
Wash the mica from step 2.4.6 and add the phage from 2.4.7.
Repeat steps 2.4.4 to 2.4.9 until the phage is negatively panned against all eight mica surfaces with immunoprecipitated protein.
Repeat step 2.1.7 using the phage after the first and eighth round of negative panning.
Immunoprecipitate TDP-43 protein from the brains of individuals with FTD.
Cleave two mica surfaces.
Add 50 μl of 10 μg/ml of FTD TDP-43 to one mica surface.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
Wash the mica 5 times with 0.1% PBST.
Add 50 μl of phage collected after negative panning against healthy TDP-43.
Incubate for 5 min.
Collect the unbound phages.
Repeat steps 2.5.3 to 2.5.6 with the second mica and the unbound phages from step 2.5.6.
Immunoprecipitate TDP-43 protein from the brains of individuals with ALS.
Cleave 3 mica surfaces.
Add 50 μl of 10 μg/ml of ALS TDP-43 to one mica.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
Wash the mica 5 times with 0.1% PBST.
Add 50 μl of the phage collected after negative panning against healthy TDP-43 to the mica.
Incubate for 5 min.
Collect the unbound phages.
Add 50 μl of trypsin (1 mg/ml in PBS) to each mica.
Incubate for no more than 10 min.
Collect the solution and save.
Add 50 μl of 100 mM triethylamine (TEA) to each mica.
Incubate for no more than 10 min.
Collect the solution, add equal volume of 1 M Tris-HCl buffer pH 7.4 and save.
Add 50 μl of TG1 at OD600 of 0.4 directly to the mica.
Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C.
Take the unbound phage collected from the previous elution methods.
Add it to the second mica with ALS TDP-43.
Incubate for 5 min.
Repeat all steps in 3.3 for these second sets of mica.
Combine TG1 cells infected with phages eluted from ALS TDP-43 mica with trypsin.
Plate the combined TG1 cells on LBA plates.
Repeat the process for TEA and TG1 cells eluted with phages from ALS TDP-43 mica.
Collect unbound phage after two rounds of negative panning against FTD TDP-43.
Use collected phage in one round of positive panning against ALS TDP-43 antigen on new mica plates.
Repeat all steps for third round of positive panning with the new ALS mica.
Plate infected TG1 cells from third round on three LBA plates overnight at 37 °C.
Count colonies on six LBA plates to identify potential ALS-specific clones.
Grow each colony from six plates in 96-well plates containing 2xYT with glucose and ampicillin overnight at 37 °C.
Transfer 10 μl from wells containing clones after the third round of positive panning to microcentrifuge tubes with 1 ml of 2xYT, 1% glucose, and 100 μg/ml ampicillin.
Add glycerol to all cultures in 96-well plates to a final concentration of 15% and freeze the plates at -80°C.
Grow 1 ml cultures for 2-3 hours shaking at 37°C.
Add 109 KM13 helper phage and allow infection for 1 hour at 37°C with shaking.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 3,000 x g; discard supernatant and add 1 ml of 2xYT with 0.1% glucose, 100 μg/ml ampicillin, and 50 μg/ml kanamycin.
Culture the cells overnight at 30°C with shaking.
Centrifuge tubes at 3,300 x g for 30 minutes; transfer supernatant to new microcentrifuge tubes and add 250 μl PEG/NaCl to each tube.
Incubate tubes on ice for 1 hour.
Centrifuge tubes again at 3,300 x g for 30 minutes; discard supernatant and add 100 μl PBS to each tube.
Incubate tubes on ice for 1 hour.
Spin the tubes for 10 minutes at 11,600 x g and transfer the supernatant to new tubes.
Store phages at -80°C.
Add 100 μl of 2.5 μg/ml of ALS, FTD, and healthy human brain tissue to the wells of a high binding ELISA plate for each potential ALS clone.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 1 hr with slow shaking.
Wash the plates 3 times with 0.1% PBST.
Add 200 μl of 2% milk powder in PBS to the well and incubate the plates at 37 °C for 1 hr with slow shaking.
Repeat the wash step.
Add 100 μl of each phage diluted at least 1/100 in PBS to the wells.
Incubate the plates and then wash them again.
Add 100 μl of 1/1,000 anti-M13 HRP to each well.
Wash the plates once more.
Visualize using the ELISA femto chemiluminescence substrate kit.
Grow HB 2151 cells to OD600 of 0.4.
Add 5 μl of different phages to 20 μl of the HB 2151 cells.
Allow the phages 30 min to infect at 37 °C without shaking.
Divide LBA plates into grids so that approximately 20 clones can be plated on each.
Add 5-10 μl of each phage infected bacteria to the plate and incubate O/N at 37 °C.
The next day, add individual colonies to 1 ml of 2xYT with 0.1% glucose and 100 μg/ml of ampicillin and shake at 37 °C for 3-4 hr until OD600 is 0.6.
Add 1 μl of 1 M IPTG to each tube and incubate O/N at 30 °C with shaking.
Spin the tubes at 11,600 x g for 10 min and harvest the supernatant for ELISA testing.
Add 10-20 μl of the target antigen to cleaved mica and incubate for 5-10 min.
Wash the mica 5 times with water.
Add 10-20 μl of the phages to the mica and incubate for 5-10 min.
Wash the mica 5 times again with water and allow the mica to air dry.
Visualize phage binding using AFM tapping mode with a Nanoscope IIIa controller in air at RT.
Use silicon AFM probes with a resonant frequency of 300 kHz and a spring constant of 40 N/m for imaging.
Set the scan rate to 3.05 Hz and the scan resolution to 512 samples/line.
Process images by basic flattening of the background to ensure particle sizes are comparable within each image.
Add 250 μg of homogenized brain tissue from motor cortex, 100 μl of anti-TDP-43 polyclonal antibody (1/100 dilution), and 700 μl of STEN buffer to an Eppendorf tube.
Incubate the mixture overnight at 4 °C on a rotator.
Wash A/G agarose beads with the STEN buffer 2-3 times.
Add 25 ml of washed A/G agarose beads to the tissue mixture and incubate for 1.5 hours at 4 °C on a rotator.
Centrifuge the mixture at 2,000-4,000 rpm for 1 minute.
Remove the supernatant and wash the pellet once with STEN buffer.
Wash the pellet five times with PBS.
Add 40-60 μl of STEN buffer to the pellet and boil for 5 minutes.
After cooling, centrifuge the samples and collect the supernatant.
Use SDS-PAGE and Western blotting to verify success of the immunoprecipitation process.
Cut nitrocellulose paper into small rectangles for each sample that will be tested.
Dot 2 μl of ALS, FTD, and healthy human brain tissue samples onto the nitrocellulose paper and let it dry completely.
Add 1-2 ml of 5% milk powder in PBS and shake for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add 1 ml of each phage (1/100 dilution) and shake overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the membrane three times for 10 minutes with 0.5% PBST.
Add 1 ml of anti-M13 HRP (1/1,000 dilution) and shake for 1 hour at room temperature.
Repeat wash procedure.
Visualize using Western chemiluminescence solution.
